summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with hypotension, lightheadedness, and new hypoxemia. He has a complex history including HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension on treprostinil, and awaiting liver transplant. Workup revealed Enterobacter bacteremia from an unclear source, likely contributing to sepsis and hypotension. He also had significant volume overload, evidenced by bilateral leg edema, bibasilar crackles, and elevated BNP, which improved with aggressive diuresis. A right heart catheterization showed mildly elevated pulmonary pressures at 25 mmHg. He responded well to IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, and was weaned off oxygen. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with pulmonology and primary care.
